faqs.q: Sec. 62-40.5. - No trespass orders for city-owned property.
faqs.a:
(a)
Legislative declaration.
The city council hereby finds and declares that it is necessary to restrict, limit,
               or revoke access to city-owned property of those persons who have been charged with
               committing an offense on that property. The issuance and enforcement of no trespass
               orders are important in reducing crime in public places and are key to promoting the
               public health, safety, and welfare. The city council also finds and declares that
               any person to whom a no trespass order has been issued must be accorded the opportunity
               to be heard as soon as is practicable.
(b)
Definitions.
As used in this section:
City
means the City of Arvada.
Court
means the Arvada municipal court, unless the context requires otherwise.
Defendant
means the person charged with committing an offense on city-owned property and to
               whom a no trespass order has been issued.
No trespass order
means any order that prohibits a person from entering or remaining on city-owned
               premises or from coming within a specified distance of those premises and that is
               issued to the person charged with an offense that occurred on the premises, or any
               order that amends, modifies, supplements, extends, or supersedes the initial no trespass
               order.
Offense
means any crime or violation punishable by law by either fine or imprisonment or
               both, and that occurs on city-owned property. For purposes of enforcement of this
               section, it does not include a traffic violation or offense committed on a public
               highway, street, or roadway.
Premises
or
property
means any real property, building, or other improvement or improvements thereon that
               is owned or leased for use by the city, including the banks and beds of any nonnavigable
               fresh water streams or creeks flowing through such real property. For purposes of
               enforcement of this section, it does not mean or include any property owned by the
               city but leased to another person or entity pursuant to a valid lease document.
(c)
Authority.
The court is authorized to hear matters related to the issuance of no trespass orders
               pursuant to this section because venue is proper in the city where the acts necessitating
               the no trespass order are alleged to have occurred. Any Arvada police officer is authorized
               by the city to serve upon a person who has been charged with any offense alleged to
               have been committed in or upon city-owned property a no trespass order.
(d)
Initiation of process.
Any person who has been charged with any offense alleged to have been committed in
               or upon city-owned property may be served with a no trespass order at any time after
               the initiation of prosecution and before the case has been closed by the court in
               which it was charged. The no trespass order shall take effect and become enforceable
               upon service.
(e)
Contents of order.
The no trespass order shall contain:
(1)
The defendant's name;
(2)
A physical description of the defendant;
(3)
The street address of the city-owned property on which the offense is alleged to have
               been committed, as well as the name by which the property is commonly known, if available.
               If no street address is known, or if the common name of the property is unavailable,
               the location shall be designated by reference to a numbered block or by the two nearest
               cross streets;
(4)
The nature of the restriction, limitation, or revocation;
(5)
Notice that the defendant must appear at the court for a status hearing at a time
               and date set not more than 14 days following service of the no trespass order for
               the purpose of allowing the defendant to request a contested hearing that will provide
               the defendant an opportunity to be heard or to otherwise contest the order;
(6)
Notice that if the defendant does not appear at the court at the time and date fixed
               by the order for a status hearing, that a contested hearing will not be held; that
               the no trespass order shall become an order of the court; and that the order shall
               remain in effect for one year from the date of service;
(7)
Notice that a violation of the no trespass order shall constitute a criminal offense
               pursuant to
section 62-40.5
of the Arvada City Code, and may subject the defendant to such punishment as may
               be provided by law; and
(8)
Notice that a third party may not give the defendant permission to violate the no
               trespass order.
(f)
Documentation to court.
The police department shall make available to the court at the earliest practicable
               time following service of the no trespass order documentation relevant to the issuance
               of the order, including a copy of the no trespass order served upon the defendant.
(g)
Status hearing.
The court shall, at the time and date set forth in the no trespass order, convene
               a status hearing during which the defendant may request a contested hearing to determine
               whether the no trespass order should be lifted, be modified in any aspect or manner,
               or remain in effect. If the defendant fails to appear for the status hearing or for
               a status hearing that has been continued for any reason, a contested hearing will
               not be held. The no trespass order shall become an order of the court, and shall remain
               in effect for one year from the date of service of the order.
(h)
Contested hearing.
If, at the status hearing, the defendant requests a contested hearing, the court
               shall convene, at a reasonable time thereafter, a contested hearing to allow the defendant
               an opportunity to be heard and respond to whether the no trespass order should be
               lifted, be modified in any aspect or manner, or remain in effect. At the contested
               hearing, the judge shall examine the record and the evidence to determine whether
               the no trespass order should be lifted, be modified in any aspect or manner, or remain
               in effect. If the defendant fails to appear for the contested hearing, or for a contesting
               hearing that has been continued for any reason, a contested hearing will not be held.
               The no trespass order shall become an order of the court, and shall remain in effect
               for one year from the date of service of the order.
(1)
Order to become order of the court.
Upon a finding that:
i.
The defendant has engaged in an activity on city-owned property which activity serves
               to impair or diminish the right or ability of the public to use and enjoy the property;
ii.
Restricting, limiting, or revoking the defendant's access to the property will serve
               to restrain, prevent, or reduce the defendant's ability to engage in the activity
               on the property; and
iii.
Issuing the no trespass order will promote the public's health, safety, and welfare;
The court shall order that the no trespass order, including any modifications, become
               an order of the court and that it shall remain in effect for one year from the date
               of service.
(2)
Standard for issuance and burden of proof.
A conviction of the offense or offenses which triggered the no trespass order is
               not required for such a finding or findings to be made. The burden of proof is by
               a preponderance of the evidence.
(3)
Advisement.
Upon issuance of an order at a hearing, the judge shall inform the defendant that
               a violation of the no trespass order shall constitute a criminal offense pursuant
               to
section 62-40.5
of the Arvada City Code. Failure of the judge to so advise the defendant shall not
               affect the validity of the order.
(i)
Continuance.
If a hearing held under this section is continued for any reason, the court shall
               immediately and in writing notify both the defendant and the city attorney's office
               of the continuance, and notify the defendant that if the defendant does not appear
               on the date and time to which the hearing has been continued, the no trespass order
               shall become an order of the court which shall remain in effect for one year from
               the date of service. The order shall remain in effect for the period of any continuance.
(j)
Length of order.
A no trespass order shall remain in effect for one (1) year from the date of service
               of the order.
Exception:
In a municipal court case which triggered the service of the no trespass order, the
               court, on its own motion or that of the city attorney, may extend the order until
               the case is closed by the court.
(k)
Entry of order.
The original no trespass order shall be kept in the court's file. The court shall
               deliver a copy of the no trespass order to the defendant if the defendant is present
               at the contested no trespass order hearing, and a copy to the records bureau of the
               police department. The court shall notify the records bureau of the police department
               any time a no trespass order is modified, extended, or dismissed.
(l)
Motion to dismiss or modify the order.
No motion to modify or dismiss a no trespass order may be filed by the defendant
               within six months of service of any no trespass order. In a case where the defendant
               is found not guilty of the offense, or all offenses, that triggered the service of
               the no trespass order, the order shall be automatically dismissed.
(m)
Not to affect rights of other property owners.
Nothing in the section shall prevent any other property owner, public or private,
               from issuing or requesting enforcement of any no trespass notice or order to any person,
               or from posting no trespassing signs upon property, or from posting signs prohibiting
               trespassing by any person on certain days or during certain times, nor shall anything
               in this section otherwise affect the rights of other property owners.
(n)
Court authority.
Nothing in this section shall be construed to alter or diminish the inherent authority
               of the court to issue or enforce no trespass or other orders through contempt proceedings
               or as otherwise authorized by law.
(o)
Collateral attack.
No person charged with violation of an order pursuant to this section shall be permitted,
               in the criminal action resulting from such charges, to collaterally attack the validity
               of the order which such person is accused of violating.
(p)
Violation and penalty.
It shall be unlawful for any person, having been served with or issued a no trespass
               order pursuant to this section that prohibits the person from entering or remaining
               on, or coming within a specified distance of a city-owned property, to enter or remain
               upon, or come within a specified distance of those premises. A person failing to comply
               with a no trespass order served or issued pursuant to this section may be prosecuted
               for a violation of this section. Violation of a no trespass order served or issued
               pursuant to this section shall be punishable by a fine or imprisonment not to exceed
               the limits established in
section 1-5
of this Code.
(q)
Civil in nature.
A no trespass order served or issued pursuant to this section shall be civil in nature.
               If issued pursuant to any municipal court case, a no trespass order may be issued
               in lieu of or in addition to any penalty specified in subsection (p).
(
Ord. No. 4277, § 1, 8-1-2011
;
Ord. No. 4833
, § 1, 12-19-2022)
